title: Masked Autoencoder (MAE)
reading: The slide walks through the Masked Autoencoder pipeline as a sequence of stages: an input image undergoes random masking of patches; only the visible patches are encoded with a Transformer encoder; the encoded latents are then expanded with learnable 'mask tokens' so the decoder sees a full-length token sequence; the decoder predicts the unknown (masked) content; and training minimises an L2 loss computed in pixel space on the masked regions. The text is essentially labels on a left-to-right pipeline figure.

visuals.description: Pipeline schematic with stage labels: random masking → encode visible patches with Transformer → expand with mask tokens → predict unknown → compute L2 loss in pixels.
visuals.assertion: MAE encodes only visible patches and reconstructs masked patches from mask tokens, supervised by pixel-space L2 loss.
